R409.note: Replaces raw NetworkStream inline-protocol write with StackExchange.Redis StringSet, so RESP length-prefixed framing prevents CRLF command injection; constructor signature change is stated and callers in the chain are unaffected.

R410.note: Normalizes destination once (toAbsolutePath+normalize) before resolving/comparing each entry, matching the stated contract exactly with no behavior change for legitimate nested entries.

R411.note: Verified in a scratch PHP 8.5 run: proc_open() with an array command blocks shell metacharacter injection (payload treated as literal, no injected command executes) and, with an empty descriptorspec, ping output still streams to stdout and proc_close still yields the exit code, matching the write-up's claims.

R412.note: Verified in a scratch Go 1.25.5 run: zero-value http.CrossOriginProtection blocks a cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site request and forged Origin, and the retained Origin check catches the no-headers legacy-request gap that Fetch-metadata-only defenses leave open; layered checks do not block the legitimate same-origin case.

R413.note: Closes classic name-based traversal (../, absolute paths) but does not reject symlink/hardlink members before validating; because all members are validated before any are extracted, a symlink member pointing outside the workspace still passes the containment check (it doesn't exist on disk yet) and, once extracted, a later member resolving through it can still write outside the workspace - the well-known tarfile Zip-Slip-via-symlink bypass this fix doesn't cover.

R414.note: sprintf -> snprintf with sizeof(line) is the standard fix; truncates rather than overflows, no other behavior change.

R415.note: Removes the shell-invoking convert entirely in favor of the sharp library, eliminating the sink; the geometry regex only enforces the WIDTHxHEIGHT format the endpoint's own doc comment already declares as the accepted input, and is required anyway since sharp needs numeric width/height.

R416.note: id = ANY($1) with the ids array bound as a single pg parameter is the standard safe replacement for a hand-built IN() list; matches the stated contract and, if anything, fixes an existing empty-array edge case rather than breaking one.

R417.note: Build FAILS: SimpleEvaluationContext has no setRootObject method (that API only exists on StandardEvaluationContext) - the file does not compile, so nothing works and this is undisclosed in the write-up.

R418.note: Adds an explicit bounds check (playerIndex >= MAX_PLAYERS) before the write, the standard fix for this class; valid indices are unaffected and out-of-range updates are dropped, which is the point of the fix, not a regression.

R419.note: Verified in a scratch JDK 26 run on Windows: Runtime.exec(String[]) with cmd.exe /c dir <data> does not let a shell metacharacter ('&') in the argument execute a second command (produces 'File Not Found' instead of running the injected echo) - the array form closes the vector on both platform branches.

R420.note: Standard SqlCommand.Parameters.Add() parameterization; preserves ExecuteNonQuery's return value and response shape.

R421.note: Fixes the reported symlink-escape vector (abspath -> realpath) but leaves the pre-existing containment check as a bare string startswith(REPORT_ROOT) with no separator; verified in a scratch run that relative_path='../reports-secret/passwd' resolves to a sibling directory yet still passes the startswith check, so the same CWE-22 sink remains exploitable via a different technique than the one named.

R422.note: Build FAILS: CS0103, SqlDbType is referenced without the System.Data using directive - does not compile, so the endpoint cannot run at all.

R423.note: Verified in a scratch .NET 10/EF Core+SQLite run: ExecuteSqlRawAsync(sql, accountId, status, beforeUtc) with literal @accountId/@status placeholders in the SQL string throws InvalidOperationException ('Must add values for the following parameters: @accountId, @status') on every call because EF Core only binds positional {0},{1},{2} placeholders for raw values, not named ones - the archive operation never succeeds, silently breaking all legitimate use, undisclosed in the write-up.
